X.note: Warm, believable weathered plaster and a convincing light and shadow split on the cobbles. The people are faceless, mannequin-like figures in clay or khaki tones, scattered evenly and standing stiffly like game-engine crowd fillers. The left wall has a blown-out yellow patch with a hard-edged rectangular glow that reads as a lighting or texture artifact. The distant flag, ship and harbour are fine. The result is a decent architectural render with weak human content.

Y.note: Richer plaster in a coral/red and ochre palette, with stone string courses and base plinths that add structure. The haze and depth are better, and the distant square fades softly. The figures are the same faceless mannequins, and they are clumped awkwardly at the right edge, overlapping, with some in odd poses. The pale haze patch in the midground looks like an empty flat area. The left-foreground figure has an odd hat and posture. It is slightly better built than X, but the crowd is still toy-like.

why: Y has more architectural detail (string courses, plinths, richer plaster variation) and better atmospheric depth, while both share the same mannequin-like crowd problem and X adds a blown-out lighting glitch on the left wall.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the plastic-looking mannequin crowd with properly modelled and textured 1943 figures: varied RN, Army and civilian clothing, faces, natural poses and groupings. Then fix the blown-out rectangular glow on the left facade and add street furniture such as signage, vehicles and shop details.
anachronisms_seen: Uniform-looking khaki and blue figures without clear 1943 insignia
Clean modern-looking steel balcony railings and uniform shutters
Pristine cobbles with no wartime wear, sandbags or blackout measures
Very modern CG-style flag and ship rendering
